result:
All 24 months are played. All three training runs were met, inference was fully served every month, and there were no penalties. **Final net cost: $1,268.1M.**

| Item | $M |
|---|---|
| GPU purchases | 910.0 |
| Cloud reservations | 419.8 |
| Power | 226.5 |
| Spot | 10.6 |
| Unserved inference | 0 |
| Resale income | −177.5 |
| Remaining contract and power obligations | +121.2 |
| End value of GPUs still held | −242.5 |
| **Net cost** | **1,268.1** |

**What I did:**
- **Month 0:** ordered the maximum 30k gen H GPUs, because the vendor's monthly shipments were the main limit on capacity. Supply was tight, so the order took until month 13 to arrive in full.
- **Months 0–3:** reserved 3 kH a month on 24-month contracts, the most providers would accept in a tight market.
- **Power:** signed 70 MW in total across months 0, 2 and 10, timed to arrive ahead of the deliveries and to cover the original 16 MW contract ending after month 19.
- **Gen N:** it launched in month 14. I bought 4k as a buffer for the final run. Inference demand stayed on the slower ~3% growth path, so I resold all of it, plus 9k gen H, in months 16–23.

**Where cost went:**
- **Too much capacity early.** The first run needed 60 kH-months and got 155; the second needed 140 and got 315. That surplus was paid for and unused. I was building toward the third run, which needed 320 by itself, and the early 24-month reservations cost the most here. A smaller first GPU order plus spot purchases would probably have come out cheaper.
- **The gen N buffer.** Buying gen N and reselling it lost about $50M net, since demand never needed the extra capacity.
- **Final run margin.** It was met with about 18 kH-months of margin projected before the last month.
